questions.q: What does a router do?
options: Directs data between networks, for example from a home network to the internet

questions.q: What is an IP address?
options: A unique number that identifies a device on a network
The name of a web browser

questions.q: What does a DNS server do?
options: Translates domain names into IP addresses

questions.q: What does a firewall do?
options: Monitors network traffic and blocks unwanted connections

questions.q: Which type of malware secretly collects information about what a user does?
Which is an advantage of a wired (Ethernet) connection compared with Wi-Fi?
options: It is cheaper to install in every case
It is usually faster and more stable
It lets you move around freely

questions.q: A switch connects devices in a LAN and sends data only to the device that needs it.
A URL and an IP address are the same thing.
questions.explain: A URL is a web address that is easy to read; an IP address is the numeric address of a device.

questions.q: Bandwidth is the amount of data that can be sent over a connection in a given time.
Using public Wi-Fi without any protection is completely safe.
A ____ address looks like 192.168.1.10.
In the URL www.school.org, the part 'school.org' is the ____ name.
Storing and accessing files over the internet instead of on your own device is called ____ storage.
A device connects to a network using a network interface ____ (NIC).
Explain the difference between a LAN and a WAN.
questions.answer: A LAN covers a small area such as a school or building (1); a WAN covers a large area, such as a country or the world, and often uses public/leased lines (1).

questions.q: Describe two ways to protect a computer from malware.
questions.answer: Any two from: install and update antivirus software; use a firewall; keep the operating system updated; do not open unknown email attachments or links; only download from trusted sites.

questions.q: Explain what phishing is and how you can recognise a phishing email.
questions.answer: Phishing is a scam that tricks people into giving away personal details such as passwords (1). Clues (any two): urgent threats; asks for personal details; suspicious link or sender address; spelling mistakes (1 mark each).

questions.q: Match each network device to its job.
pairs: Lets a device connect to a network

questions.q: Match each type of malware to its description.
pairs: Attaches itself to files and spreads when they are shared
Pretends to be useful software but does harm
Secretly records what the user does

questions.q: The web address is https://www.school.org/contact. Match each part to its meaning.
pairs: The protocol (secure way of sending data)
The path to a page on the site
